verses.text: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and his disciples:
“The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
So do what they tell you to observe, but don’t copy what they do. They talk about it but don’t follow through.
They tie up heavy burdens that are hard to carry and put them on people’s shoulders, but they won’t lift a finger to help.
They do everything to be noticed. They make their scripture boxes wide and their robe fringes long.
They love the places of honor at banquets and the best seats in the synagogues.
They love being greeted in the marketplaces and being called ‘Rabbi’ by people.
But don’t let people call you ‘Rabbi,’ because you have one Teacher, the Messiah, and you’re all siblings.
Don’t call anyone on earth your father, because you have one Father in heaven.
And don’t let people call you masters, because you have one Master, the Messiah.
The greatest among you must be your servant.
Whoever lifts themselves up will be brought low, and whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You take over widows’ homes while pretending to pray long prayers. Because of this, your judgment will be more severe.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the Kingdom of Heaven in people’s faces. You don’t enter yourselves, and you stop those who are trying to enter.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You travel across sea and land to make one convert. When you do, you make that person twice as fit for Gehenna as you are.
“How terrible for you, blind guides! You say, ‘If someone swears by the temple, it means nothing. But if they swear by the temple’s gold, they’re bound by the oath.’
You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes the gold sacred?
You also say, ‘If someone swears by the altar, it means nothing. But if they swear by the gift on it, they’re bound by the oath.’
You blind fools! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes the gift sacred?
So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and everything on it.
Whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who lives in it.
Whoever swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the one who sits on it.

“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You give a tenth of your mint, dill, and cumin, but you’ve neglected the more important things in the Law: justice, mercy, and faith. You should have done these without neglecting the others.
You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and plate, but inside they’re full of extortion and wrongdoing.
Blind Pharisee, clean the inside of the cup and plate first, so the outside can be clean too.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You’re like whitewashed tombs: beautiful on the outside, but inside full of dead people’s bones and every kind of uncleanness.
In the same way, you look righteous to people on the outside, but inside you’re full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
“How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the graves of righteous people.
You say, ‘If we’d lived in the days of our ancestors, we wouldn’t have helped them kill the prophets.’
By saying that, you testify against yourselves that you’re descendants of those who killed the prophets.
Go ahead, then—complete the full measure of your ancestors’ sins.
You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
That’s why I’m sending you prophets, wise people, and scribes. Some you’ll kill and crucify; some you’ll whip in your synagogues and chase from town to town.
So all the righteous blood shed on earth will come upon you, from righteous Abel’s blood to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
I’m telling you the truth: all these things will come upon this generation.
“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How many times I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathering her chicks under her wings, but you refused.
Look, your house is left to you deserted.
I tell you, you won’t see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name!’”
